data.name: Children of the Nile: Alexandria
data.detailed_description:
Children of the Nile: Alexandria é um complemento do jogo base Children of the Nile, adicionando um novo modo mini-campanha focado na ascensão da cidade de Alexandria.

Usando a técnica dinâmica de construção de cidade de Children of the Nile, podes esculpir uma nova dinastia para governar todo o Egipto, e construir a maior cidade do mundo antigo! Cada pessoa na tua cidade é uma pessoa totalmente desenvolvida, com desejos e necessidades. Cuida das suas necessidades e elas trabalharão para ti para que possas criar um império poderoso e um legado duradouro.

Em Alexandria, podes tomar o papel dos novos Faraós do Egipto, numa mini-campanha com três cenários, durante e após as etapas finais das conquistas de Alexandre o Grande. Consolida o teu poder enquanto os antigos tenentes de Alexandre disputam pelo controlo do seu império, tudo isto enquanto desenvolves uma nova capital egípcia e constróis novos grandes monumentos: O Grande Farol e a Grande Biblioteca de Alexandria!

reviews.review:
Don't be deterred by the age of this game.   I'm running it on a pretty newish PC and it runs better than I remember it did  back when i played it brand new on my old Pentium III.   

The graphics are antiquated now, but they're NOT bad.  Just old.   The real amazing thing about this game is the deep, rich simulation.  

Every character has a name, and belongs to a family.  They have relatives; they may move up or down the social ladder even, depending on the whims of fate.   Shopkeepers are all craftspeople, they have to procure raw materials, and then make the goods they sell.   Farmers walk down to the field and physically farm it.   Housewives actually go to the market to do the shopping;  rich ones will have servants in tow to carry their loot.   

The currency in this game is food.  Not really unlike the very first agrarian civilizations.  Government employees get their pay check from the royal bakeries.  

Depending on the scenarios, there's a wider world out there too to interact with; traders, raiders, and even colonies and things of that--that is all there.   Caravans may come, bringing luxuries like spices, incense, exotic animals, and furs.   

Of course the real goal of every Egyptian King is their tomb.   It was famously a sort of obsession for them.   And you will build many monuments, tombs, and pyramids.   Brick by brick, block by block.  

Your overseers will supervise workers, who will quarry the stone for obelisks, statues, stele and pyramids.   They will haul the stone to the building site; and THEN you will need your masons to come and finish the job.   

For the age of this simulation, the level of detail in it is mind-boggling;  I don't think the game ever truly got the credit it deserved for this.   

If you like detailed simulations, city builders, and/or ancient civilizations, check it out.  You might really like this!
